gaps.sentence: You ___ have worried — everything turned out fine.
gaps.hint: the worry was unnecessary in the end
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have' means the action happened but was unnecessary: needn't have.

gaps.sentence: I am afraid you ___ park here without a resident's permit.
gaps.hint: permission that is refused with cannot

gaps.sentence: Library books ___ be taken out of the reading room.
gaps.hint: a passive prohibition with mustn't be
gaps.explanation: Prohibitions can be passive: mustn't be taken.

gaps.sentence: If you want a refund, you ___ keep the receipt — no receipt, no refund.
gaps.hint: a necessity that applies in the future
gaps.explanation: Future necessity uses 'will have to': will have to keep.

gaps.sentence: You ___ use my office while I am on holiday.
Luckily I ___ find a parking space right outside the theatre.
gaps.hint: one particular success on that occasion
gaps.explanation: One particular success takes 'was able to': was able to find.

gaps.sentence: I ___ rather stay at home tonight, if that is all right.
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather' expresses preference: would rather stay.

gaps.sentence: Employees ___ use company computers for personal downloads.
gaps.hint: a formal prohibition with may not
gaps.explanation: Formal rules use 'may not' (or 'must not') for prohibitions: may not.
